NONE: › to not now have an unwanted or unpleasant task, object, or person
擺脫掉…；免去…的負擔
B1 to remove or throw away something unwanted
清除；除去；丟棄
B1 to sell an old or unwanted possession
處理掉；賣掉
C1 to send away someone annoying or to persuade them to leave
趕走，打發走，擺脫（某人）

example: I didn't enjoy marking those papers and I was glad to be rid of them.
我不喜歡批改那些卷子，所以我很高興能免去這一麻煩。

More examplesHave you got anything for getting rid of scuff marks on shoes?We can't sell the house because we can't get rid of the sitting tenants.The idea of the game is to get rid of all your cards as soon as you can.The horses swished their tails to get rid of the flies hovering around them.We had to sluice out the garage to get rid of the smell of petrol.
get rid of sth
That cream got rid of my skin rash.
那種藥膏治好了我身上的皮疹。
I used weedkiller to get rid of the weeds in the garden.
我用了除草劑來除去花園裡的雜草。
Have you managed to get rid of your old Volvo yet?
你處理掉你的舊富豪車了嗎？
We got rid of our unwelcome guests by saying we had to go to bed.
我們說必須要上床睡覺了，這才把那一幫不受歡迎的客人打發走。

NONE: › to cause someone or something to be free of an unpleasant or harmful thing or person
使…擺脫；從…清除；使…去除

example: Our aim is to rid this government of corruption.
我們的目的就是要消除這屆政府中的腐敗現象。

NONE: › said when you are pleased that a bad or unwanted thing or person, or something of poor quality, has gone
總算擺脫了，終於走掉了

example: We've got rid of the old computer system, and good riddance is what I say.
我們已經卸掉了舊的電腦系統，我得說謝天謝地，可算是去掉了大包袱。

NONE: › past participle of
ride verb
› full of something unpleasant or bad
充滿…的；滿是…的

example: It is a superstition-ridden community.
這個社區迷信盛行。
She was guilt-ridden when she discovered that the business had failed because of her.
當發現公司是因為自己的緣故而垮掉的時候，她內心充滿了自責。

C: › [ C ] a type of question that describes something in a difficult and confusing way and has a clever or funny answer, often asked as a game
C usually singular: › [ C usually singular ] something that is confusing, or a problem that is difficult to solve

NONE: › to make a lot of holes in something
使布滿洞孔

example: Scientists may have solved the riddle of Saturn's rings.
科學家們或許已經揭開了土星環的奧秘。
The anti-aircraft guns riddled the plane's wings with bullets.
高射炮炮彈把機翼打得千瘡百孔。

NONE: › full of holes
布滿洞孔的

example: He wore an old jacket riddled with holes.
他穿了一件滿是破洞的舊外套。

I or T: A1 [ I or T ] to sit on something such as a bicycle, motorbike, or horse and travel along on it controlling its movements
A2 [ I or T ] to travel in a vehicle, such as a car, bus, or train
T: › [ T ] US to try to control someone and force them to work
駕馭，試圖控制（某人）並強迫其工作

NONE: B1 a journey on a horse or bicycle, or in a vehicle
（騎馬、騎車或乘坐車輛的）旅行，行程
B1 mainly US UK usually lift a free journey in a car to a place where you want to go
乘便車；搭乘免費車
› US a person who gives you a ride in their car
讓你搭便車的人
› US informal someone's car
（某人的）車
B1 a machine in an amusement park that people travel in or are moved around by for entertainment
（遊樂園裡）供人乘坐的遊樂裝置

example: I learned to ride a bike when I was six.
我六歲學會了騎腳踏車。
I ride my moped to work.
我騎機器腳踏車去上班。
I ride to work on my moped.
我騎機器腳踏車去上班。
The hunters came riding by/past on their horses.
獵人們騎馬飛馳而過。
Can you ride?
你會騎馬嗎？
Their daughter is learning to ride.
他們的女兒正在學騎馬。
He rides well/badly.
他騎術很好／差。
He doesn't have a car so he rides to work on the bus.
他沒有私家車，所以就坐公車去上班。
mainly US We rode the train from San Diego to Portland.
我們從聖地牙哥坐火車到波特蘭。
Your boss is riding you much too hard at the moment.
你的老闆現在把你管得太嚴了。
It's a short bus ride to the airport.
坐公共汽車去機場很近。
I went for a (horse) ride last Saturday.
上週六我（騎馬）去兜了一圈。
Do you want to come for a ride on my bike?
你想坐我的機車去兜兜風嗎？
He asked me for a ride into town.
他請求搭我的便車進城。
Well, I have to go - my ride is here.
好了，我得走了。讓我搭車的人已經來了。
Hey, nice ride.
哎，好車。
We went on all the rides.
我們玩了遊樂園裡所有的裝置。
My favourite ride is the Ferris wheel.
我最愛坐摩天輪。

NONE: › If you ride (on) a wave of a feeling, you get an advantage from it.
乘…之勢；借…的東風

example: The new president is riding (on) a wave of popularity.
新總統深得人心，大獲其益。

NONE: › to manage not to be destroyed, harmed, or permanently affected by the difficult situation you experience
渡過難關；走出困境

example: The government seems confident that it will ride out the storm.
政府好像很有信心渡過難關。

NONE: › to be responsible for controlling a group of people and their actions
看管，監督

example: The new editor will ride herd on the staff, checking on the overall policy and tone of the paper.
新編輯將要管理全體職員，檢查該份報紙的整體政策和風格。

NONE: › When something important, such as your reputation or money, rides on a particular person or thing, it will be won or achieved if that person or thing is successful.
依賴，依靠，指望

example: The future of the company now rides on the new managing director.
公司的未來現在就指望新任經理了。
I have a lot of money riding on that horse (= I will win or lose a lot of money if that horse wins or loses the race).
我在那匹賽馬上押了很多錢。

NONE: › to do what you want without giving any attention to other people or their wishes
不管…而一意孤行

example: They accused the government of riding roughshod over parliamentary procedure.
他們指責政府藐視議會程式一意孤行。

NONE: › to continue to exist during a difficult situation and until it ends, without serious harm
安然渡過（難關）
› If a ship rides out a period of bad weather, it continues to float during it, without serious damage.
（船）平安渡過（暴風雨）

example: Many companies did not manage to ride out the recession.
經濟衰退時期，許多公司沒能渡過難關。
The ship managed to ride out the storm.
這艘輪船平安渡過了風暴。

NONE: › If a piece of clothing rides up, it moves up out of position
（衣服）向上收，縮上去

example: Your skirt has ridden up at the back.
你的裙子後面縮上去了。

NONE: › to begin a new, happy life at the end of a story
（在故事的結尾）開始幸福的新生活

example: At the end of the film, the two of them ride off into the sunset.
在電影的結尾，他們倆過上了幸福的新生活。

C: B1 a person who travels along on a horse or bicycle
› formal a statement that is added to what has already been said or decided, or an addition to a government bill (= a written plan for a law)
附加意見；附文；議案的附加條款

example: One of the riders was thrown off his horse.
其中一位騎師被甩下馬背。
I should like to add a rider to the judgment of the court.
我要在法庭判決上附加一條意見。

NONE: › without a person riding
無人騎乘的

example: a riderless horse
一匹無人騎乘的馬

NONE: › the number of passengers on a public transport system
（公共交通系統的）乘客數，乘客量

example: This month ridership on the Chicago subway went down again.
本月芝加哥地鐵的乘客量又下降了。

NONE: › a long, narrow raised part of a surface, especially a high edge along a mountain
脊；壟；（尤指）山脊
› the part of a roof where the sloping sides join at the top
屋脊

example: We walked along the narrow mountain ridge.
我們沿著狹窄的山脊行進。
figurative A ridge (= a narrow area) of high pressure will bring good weather this afternoon.
今天下午高壓脊將會帶來好天氣。

NONE: › unkind words or actions that make someone or something look stupid
嘲笑；奚落；戲弄
› to laugh at someone in an unkind way
嘲笑；奚落；戲弄

example: She was treated with scorn and ridicule by her colleagues when she applied for the job.
她申請那份工作時，受到了同事們的嘲弄和奚落。
He's become an object of ridicule (= a person that everyone thinks is stupid and criticizes or laughs at).
他成了眾人嘲弄的對象。
She rarely spoke her mind out of fear of being ridiculed.
她怕人嘲笑，幾乎從來不說出自己的想法。
He was ridiculed for his ideas.
他因為自己的想法而受到嘲笑。

NONE: B2 stupid or unreasonable and deserving to be laughed at
愚蠢的；荒唐的；可笑的

example: Do I look ridiculous in this hat?
我戴這頂帽子看著很可笑嗎？
Don't be so ridiculous! I can't possibly afford to stay in a hotel like that.
別傻了！我才住不起那樣的旅館呢。
It's ridiculous to expect a two-year-old to be able to read!
指望一個兩歲的孩子能閱讀真是太荒唐了！

NONE: › the sport or activity of riding horses
騎馬（運動或活動）

example: Have you ever been riding?
你騎過馬嗎？
She goes riding on Saturdays.
她週六去騎馬。
